A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Rate-In research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons support a complete assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic regression, medical image classification, and segmentation experiments in Section 4, with additional analyses and runtime measurements in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their results, including Tables 1–7 and the supplementary analyses in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The layer-wise dropout adjustment procedure, Algorithm 1, MI and SSIM formulations, and implementation pseudocode are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate synthetic sine regression, PathMNIST, BloodMNIST, TissueMNIST, prostate MRI segmentation, and liver/tumor CT segmentation. The supplementary test scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain constant, scheduled, and activation-based dropout comparators. Table 7 retains the same MI-versus-SSIM comparison; the bibliography revisions introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The architectures, training settings, 30 Monte Carlo passes, dropout thresholds, preprocessing, and evaluation metrics remain identical, including the settings in Appendix A.

E4.justification: Both retain the same noise and sample-size sweeps, initialization/convergence analysis, layer-sensitivity analysis, runtime studies, qualitative uncertainty maps, and MI-versus-SSIM evaluation.

E5.justification: Both disclose the same synthetic-training random seed of 123 and the same mean/standard-deviation runtime reporting in Tables 4–6. No statistical reporting procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and the plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains TissueMNIST Rate-In accuracy of 0.68 and AUARC of 0.84 at dropout rate 0.05.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, dropout schedules, information-loss expressions, metric formulas, and Appendix B complexity derivation are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and summary retain the same claims about unsupervised inference-time adaptation and improved uncertainty estimation while preserving predictive performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including decoder sensitivity, convergence failures, computational overhead, MI limitations, empirical loss-threshold selection, and dropout's restricted noise coverage.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, software, hardware, and the repository link are unchanged. The corrected Decathlon citation changes a source pointer without changing the described resources or access instructions.

R1.justification: The BUC discussion replaces references to Konyushkova, Blankevoort, and Roy with works by Mehrtash and Li; Yue remains cited. Section 6.2.2 also corrects the Decathlon citation. The broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds Meta FAIR as Yann LeCun's affiliation and updates citation references and the version header. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised bibliography reflows across PDF pages 8–9, with small citation-related text shifts elsewhere. All figures, tables, captions, and their placements remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Section 6.2.2 corrects its citation for the Medical Segmentation Decathlon: v1 points to 'Segment anything in medical images,' whereas v3 points to the named Decathlon paper. This provides a limited improvement in source traceability. The scientific methods, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
